method: Encode: pick the 6° UTM zone with the Norway exception (56°N to 64°N, 3°E to 12°E uses zone 32) and the four Svalbard exceptions (72°N to 84°N uses zones 31, 33, 35 and 37), then the latitude band C to X, which is eight degrees tall except X at twelve. Project on the WGS84 ellipsoid with the transverse Mercator series at a central scale of 0.9996, a 500,000 m false easting and a 10,000,000 m false northing south of the equator. The 100 km square is the easting column letter from the eight-letter set chosen by zone mod 3 (ABCDEFGH for 1, JKLMNPQR for 2, STUVWXYZ for 0) plus the northing row letter from the twenty-letter cycle A to V without I and O, which repeats every 2,000,000 m and shifts five letters for even zones. Digits after the square are whole metres inside the square, truncated rather than rounded, so five digits each side names a 1 m cell and each fewer digit coarsens the cell tenfold down to the bare 100 km square. Decode reverses the projection, rebuilds the missing 2,000,000 m northing cycle from the latitude band and reports the centre of the named cell together with its corners. Zones 32X, 34X and 36X do not exist. Coverage stops at 80°S and 84°N, no datum transformation is applied (the reference is WGS84 MGRS), the series is accurate to roughly a metre, digits are truncated rather than rounded, and the result is a grid reference rather than a statement about position accuracy.

sources.title: MGRS is built from UTM: 6° zones, latitude bands C to X omitting I and O, 100 km square letters, and northing row letters that repeat every 2,000,000 m (NGA, Military Grid Reference System)
Band X spans 72°N to 84°N, Norway reassigns 56°N to 64°N and 3°E to 12°E to zone 32, and Svalbard uses zones 31, 33, 35 and 37 without 32X, 34X or 36X (NGA, UTM zone exceptions)
MGRS easting and northing digits truncate the position, so a reference names the south-west corner of the square it names and never rounds up into the next square (NGA, MGRS truncation rule)
